headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write files and use allowlisted egress while great_expectations reads/writes data-quality artifacts, creating default-path leakage and output-chaining risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can operate on the filesystem and call agent protocol APIs, while great_expectations reads/writes validation files and documentation. A direct injection path is plausible if one agent consumes the other's files, but no shared channel is documented and great_expectations has no network egress. This is lower than medium because the bridge is not shown by the profiles.
conditions: IF AutoGPT reads great_expectations-generated files as instructions
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace
IF an operator copy-pastes validation text from great_expectations into AutoGPT prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents into prompts
Use read-only mounts for great_expectations outputs
Require human review before AutoGPT acts on external text

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress, while great_expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation. If they share a workspace, sensitive validation artifacts can flow from great_expectations into AutoGPT and then out through AutoGPT's egress. The profiles do not prove sensitive data classes, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem path
IF validation results contain sensitive source data
IF AutoGPT is allowed to transmit file-derived context over its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Use separate directories with strict permissions
Redact validation outputs before AutoGPT can read them
Block AutoGPT egress for runs that touch sensitive datasets
Store great_expectations artifacts in a non-shared location

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and great_expectations can install packages and manipulate files. On a shared mutable workspace, their writes can collide even though great_expectations is not itself networked. The profiles do not show locking or orchestration, so overlapping write capability is the main conflict.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF package installation or shell actions modify shared environment state
IF no external lock or scheduler serializes their runs
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run package installs in isolated environments
Serialize access with a simple lock file
Make shared artifacts append-only

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from files and APIs, and great_expectations is a validation tool that may treat upstream artifacts as authoritative inputs. If AutoGPT's generated text or files feed great_expectations without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect validation results or downstream decisions. The profiles do not show a verification step, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF great_expectations consumes AutoGPT-produced files as test inputs
IF no human or schema verification occurs between agents
IF downstream automation trusts validation results without review
mitigations: Insert a schema check between agents
Require human approval before validation runs
Keep AutoGPT outputs in a staging folder
Compare results against a known-good baseline

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no requested secrets or explicit residency constraints. great_expectations touches validation results and documentation, while AutoGPT has allowlisted egress, so compliance risk exists only if regulated data is routed through the pair. The profiles do not evidence a specific residency or certification mismatch, so this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into great_expectations artifacts
IF AutoGPT is used to transmit those artifacts across a restricted boundary
IF the deployment has residency or retention requirements
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through shared artifacts
Document retention for validation outputs
Restrict AutoGPT egress on regulated runs
Keep compliance-sensitive datasets out of the pair
